primitives.name: Scrimmage
primitives.verbatim_quote: A Scrimmage takes place when the holder of the ball places it flat upon the ground, with its long axis at right angles to the line of scrimmage, and puts it in play by snapping it back.
primitives.assumptions: The ball is snapped from a stationary position on the ground with a single continuous motion; the long axis of the ball is held perpendicular to the line of scrimmage.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If the snapper-back fails to maintain the proper orientation of the ball's long axis, the snap is invalid and must be reattempted.

layer2.mapping: GSE: The scrimmage defines the core state-transition event where the ball changes possession status, triggering the start of a new play clock. GSI: The probability distribution over possible outcomes (e.g., yards gained) is conditioned on the initial state of the ball at the line of scrimmage.
layer2.telemetry: Time-to-snap (in seconds) and spatial coordinates of the ball's release point.

primitives.name: Free-kick
primitives.verbatim_quote: A Free-kick is any kick when the·opponents are restrained by rule from advancing beyond a certain point before the ball is put in play, and includes Kick-off, Punt-out, Kick from a Fair Catch, and Place-kick for Goal after a touchdown.
primitives.assumptions: All free-kicks enforce a 'no-advance' restriction on opponents until the ball is legally put into play, preventing interference during the kick.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs if an opponent breaches the restricted zone before the ball is kicked, resulting in a foul and potential loss of yardage.

layer2.mapping: GSE: Free-kicks establish a fixed state transition from one team's possession to the other's, often used strategically to reset field position. GSI: The expected value of field position after a free-kick depends on the probability distribution of return distance, modeled via conformal prediction intervals.
layer2.telemetry: Distance traveled by the ball post-kick and time elapsed until the ball becomes dead.

primitives.name: Line of Scrimmage
primitives.verbatim_quote: The Line of Scrimmage for each side is an imaginary line parallel to the goal line Line of Scrimmage.
primitives.assumptions: Each team has a distinct Line of Scrimmage that serves as the reference point for measuring forward progress and enforcing offside rules.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Violations occur when players cross their respective Lines of Scrimmage prematurely, leading to penalties that adjust the effective starting position of the next play.

layer2.mapping: GSE: The Line of Scrimmage delineates the boundary between the offensive and defensive zones, dictating which players can engage in blocking or tackling. GSI: Positional data relative to the Line of Scrimmage is used to compute probabilities of successful downs conversion using Bayesian hierarchical models.
layer2.telemetry: X and Y coordinates of the Line of Scrimmage and player positions relative to it.

primitives.name: Snap
primitives.verbatim_quote: Snapping the ball is putting it back from its position on the ground with one quick and continuous motion of the hand or hands, the ball actually leaving the hands on this motion.
primitives.assumptions: The snap must be executed in a single, uninterrupted motion without hesitation, ensuring a clean transfer of momentum to initiate the play.
primitives.breakdown_regime: A fumble results if the snap is too slow, allowing defenders to recover the loose ball before it reaches the intended receiver.

layer2.mapping: GSE: The snap triggers the start of a play clock and initiates the sequence of events leading to either a run or pass. GSI: Timing metrics derived from the snap (e.g., time-to-snap) are predictive features in machine learning models for classifying play type and outcome.
layer2.telemetry: Velocity vector of the ball immediately post-snap and duration of the snap motion.
